findings.title: Request-level ssl_context overrides adapter's custom ssl_context
findings.suggested_fix: In _urllib3_request_context (or in HTTPAdapter._get_connection) only set pool_kwargs['ssl_context'] = _preloaded_ssl_context when the adapter's poolmanager/connection_pool_kw does not already contain an ssl_context (e.g. check self.poolmanager.connection_pool_kw.get('ssl_context') / proxy_manager kw), otherwise leave pool_kwargs untouched so the user's context wins.

findings.title: Client cert loaded onto shared module-level SSLContext
findings.suggested_fix: Only use the shared context when client_cert is None: change the branch to `elif verify is True and client_cert is None:` (or otherwise fall back to the per-pool context path, leaving cert_file/key_file to urllib3's own context) so load_cert_chain never runs on the shared object.

residual_risks: The preloaded context is now built at import time (create_urllib3_context + load_verify_locations(extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH))); a missing or unreadable CA bundle (stripped certifi, frozen apps) now fails `import requests` instead of raising the lazy OSError in cert_verify, and later monkeypatching of DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH / requests.certs.where no longer affects verify=True.

urllib3 mutates the shared context per connection (verify_mode, and check_hostname=False when adapter pool kwargs set assert_hostname/assert_fingerprint), so per-adapter settings can leak process-wide across verify=True connections; adapter-level ssl_version/ssl_minimum_version pool kwargs are ignored when ssl_context is supplied.
testing_gaps: No test covers an HTTPAdapter subclass supplying its own ssl_context with verify=True, nor a verify=True + cert request followed by a certless request to confirm the shared context is not mutated.

findings.title: Shared SSLContext accumulates client certs across requests (CWE-284/CWE-501)
findings.suggested_fix: In _urllib3_request_context, use the shared context only when no client cert is given: `elif verify is True and client_cert is None: pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context`; when verify is True and client_cert is not None, fall back to pool_kwargs["ca_certs"] = extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH) (and in cert_verify set conn.ca_certs to that default path when cert is supplied), so each cert-bearing connection builds its own context as before. Assumption: mTLS requests accept the per-connection load_verify_locations cost.

residual_risks: Any other per-connection state urllib3 writes into the shared context persists process-wide: verify_mode (always CERT_REQUIRED on this path, benign) and check_hostname, which is set False permanently when a custom adapter passes assert_hostname/assert_fingerprint via init_poolmanager. urllib3 2.8.0 falls back to its own _match_hostname when context.check_hostname is False, so hostname verification is not lost there; behaviour on older urllib3 (>=1.21.1 is allowed by setup.py) was not verified.

Custom adapters that supply their own ssl_context through pool kwargs get it overridden by the shared context for verify=True (pool_kwargs override base pool kwargs), silently dropping their custom ciphers/min TLS version/CA pinning; not verified against upstream semantics, and it is a behaviour change rather than a verification bypass.
The shared context is mutated concurrently (set_alpn_protocols, verify_mode, load_cert_chain) from many threads without a lock; only the load_cert_chain case has a security consequence.
testing_gaps: No test asserts that a cert= request does not leave the client certificate on the shared context (e.g., after a cert= request, _preloaded_ssl_context must not present a cert to a later cert-less request).
No test covers concurrent requests with different client certs against a mutual-TLS server.

findings.title: New verify routing in adapters has no test coverage
findings.suggested_fix: Add a parametrized unit test in tests/test_adapters.py calling requests.adapters._urllib3_request_context(PreparedRequest for https URL, verify, None) asserting: True -> pool_kwargs['ssl_context'] is requests.adapters._preloaded_ssl_context and no ca_certs/ca_cert_dir; False -> cert_reqs CERT_NONE and no CA keys; existing file path (e.g. tests/certs/valid/ca/ca.crt) -> ca_certs; tmp_path directory -> ca_cert_dir. Add a cert_verify test with a mock conn asserting ca_certs/ca_cert_dir untouched for verify=True and ca_cert_dir set for a directory.

residual_risks: The import-time preloading of the default CA bundle (including the extract_zipped_paths zipped-bundle case) has no test; a failure there would surface as an ImportError of requests.adapters rather than a request-time error.

Env-derived failures at base (expired test certs, missing Authority Key Identifier) mean test_different_connection_pool_for_mtls_settings also fails locally (SSLV3_ALERT_CERTIFICATE_EXPIRED on the client cert), further reducing effective TLS-path coverage here; this is environmental, not caused by the diff.
testing_gaps: No test that a verify=True request succeeds through the preloaded ssl_context against a server whose CA is in the default bundle (would need network or patching the module context); current verify=True coverage is only a negative SSLError case.

findings.title: Client cert= loaded into shared SSLContext leaks to later cert-less requests
findings.suggested_fix: In _urllib3_request_context, set pool_kwargs["ssl_context"] = _preloaded_ssl_context only when verify is True and client_cert is None; otherwise leave ssl_context unset so urllib3 builds a private context and loads the default CA bundle (or fall back to ca_certs=extract_zipped_paths(DEFAULT_CA_BUNDLE_PATH)). Add a test that a request with cert= followed by one without does not present the client cert.

findings.title: Adapter subclass's custom ssl_context silently overridden by shared context for verify=True
findings.suggested_fix: Make the shared context a fallback: at the point where pool_kwargs are built (_urllib3_request_context callers in HTTPAdapter.send path) only inject _preloaded_ssl_context when the adapter's poolmanager.connection_pool_kw has no ssl_context (e.g. pool_kwargs.setdefault against self.poolmanager.connection_pool_kw), keeping the user's context when supplied.

findings.title: import requests now raises if the default CA bundle is missing or unreadable
findings.suggested_fix: Load lazily on first use (functools.lru_cache'd getter called from _urllib3_request_context) or wrap the import-time load in try/except OSError and fall back to no shared context, letting cert_verify/urllib3 raise at request time as before. Lazy creation also keeps the OSError message about the missing bundle.

findings.title: Adapter-level ca_certs now loaded into the shared context, trusted process-wide
findings.suggested_fix: Same root fix as the client-cert finding: never hand the shared context to a connection that carries additional TLS material. Alternatively skip the shared ssl_context whenever the adapter's connection_pool_kw contains ca_certs/ca_cert_dir/ca_cert_data/cert_file, or have urllib3 receive a copy (copy.copy is not supported for SSLContext, so build per-pool contexts lazily instead).
findings.first_evidence: src/requests/adapters.py:298 -- conn.cert_reqs = "CERT_REQUIRED"   (the old `conn.ca_certs = cert_loc` reset for verify=True was removed)

residual_risks: Thread interleaving of concurrent cert= requests with different client certs on the shared context (load_cert_chain then handshake are not atomic) was reasoned from urllib3 code but not reproduced with a timing experiment.

assert_hostname=False set at adapter level flips check_hostname=False on the shared context permanently; urllib3 falls back to its own _match_hostname for later connections so verification still happens, but the behavior depends on urllib3 internals (and on pyOpenSSL/IS_PYOPENSSL paths, not exercised here).
Fork: the shared context is inherited by forked children; OpenSSL SSL_CTX state is copied so this is likely benign, but not exercised.
testing_gaps: No test asserts that a request with cert= does not affect subsequent cert-less verify=True requests (shared-context isolation).
No test covers a custom ssl_context supplied via an HTTPAdapter subclass combined with verify=True, or import behavior when the CA bundle path is missing.
